subject: Post-demo: BrightCart SLOs & benchmark methodology
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma@brightcart.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hayes <thomas.hayes@brightcart.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + near-term asks

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team liked the streaming example and the cost/latency tradeoff dashboard. Quick recap and asks from our side so we can align on a short qualification runway: 

- Our primary SLOs: 150ms p95 for single-turn generation (chat completion), and sustainable throughput of 250 requests/sec for the catalog search workload.
- Streaming: we need token-level streaming with <60ms chunking for the UI; client expects incremental tokens every ~50 tokens.
- Concurrency: expected steady-state concurrency 24 per user-facing node, peak 120 across the fleet.

Action items for Redwood:
1) Share the benchmark harness and the measurement definitions you use for p95 (what counts as a request boundaries, warm vs cold KV cache).
2) Can you confirm whether prefix/KV caching will be part of the qualification run and how it will be configured?
3) We'll send a sanitized prompt set for you to run. Is there an expected format and size?

I attached a starter prompt_set (brightcart_prompt_set_v1.csv) — it includes 250 sanitized prompts representative of our search+assist path. We'll iterate if you need different coverage.

Tom and I are available next week to join any dry-run.

Thanks,
Emma Li
Director, Engineering
BrightCart

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma@brightcart.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + near-term asks

Emma — really appreciate the clear SLO targets. High-level confirmation and proposed approach below.

- Latency: 150ms p95 single-turn is aggressive but achievable on the model families we discussed with the right quantization and KV-cache warmup. We'll run dedicated qualification runs to measure p50/p95/p99 and tail behavior under concurrency.
- Throughput/concurrency: we'll map your 250 rps target into capacity (GPUs + batching profile) and report expected saturation point. We'll also test with 24 steady-state concurrency and a 120 peak spike to validate graceful degradation/fallback.
- Streaming: Ben will validate chunk interval targets. Our runtime supports configurable chunking; we'll aim for <60ms per chunk at your target load but want to confirm exact tokenization behavior on your prompt set.

What we'll share by EOD: the benchmark harness instructions (redwood_harness_instructions_v2.md), measurement definitions (how we measure p95, how we account for streaming latency vs final token), and an SLA draft (sla-draft-150ms-p95.pdf) that codifies test acceptance criteria.

Open questions for you (so Ben and Marissa can scope the runs):
1) Prompt ownership: can BrightCart confirm which prompts are canonical for acceptance vs exploratory prompts for edge-case discovery? (We prefer a separate "acceptance" bucket of ~100 queries.)
2) KV cache assumptions: do you expect cold-start per request or can we seed the cache with representative prefixes?
3) Failure budget: what's the acceptable permitted p95 misses during peak testing?

Next steps: Ben will propose a test matrix and Marissa will follow up on timeline and required infra access. If that works I'll set up a brief dry-run call next Tue.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma@brightcart.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + near-term asks

Emma / Stephanie — jumping in with a technical checklist and recommended measurement spec. See inline — I attached the harness guide and a short csv of our expected prompt import schema.

-- Measurement definitions (short):
* Request boundary: we define a request as the pair (prompt + system messages + function calls if any). For streaming, the streaming latency is measured from request receive -> first-byte-out (stream start) and full-response latency is request receive -> final token emitted. p95 values will be reported for both metrics.
* Warm vs cold: warm = KV cache populated with the last 5k tokens representative of the session; cold = empty KV cache. We'll run both and flag which dataset is used for the acceptance run.
* Concurrency/throughput: we will run fixed-concurrency tests (24 steady-state) and linear ramp tests to find the 95% throughput point.

-- Harness notes and assumptions:
* Input format: CSV with columns {id, system_prompt, user_prompt, expected_length_estimate, category_tag}. See brightcart_prompt_set_v1.csv for your layout. Our harness will accept that format and will also take a gzipped tar of prompt sets for larger runs.
* Sampling: For acceptance, we'll use a 100-query "acceptance" bucket you confirm. The remaining prompts will be exploratory to surface regression cases.
* Tokenization note: streaming chunk timing is affected by tokenization length. For the UI <60ms target, we recommend setting chunk_size to 40 tokens and enabling incremental flush (we will simulate network jitter).

-- Run matrix (proposed):
1) Warm cache acceptance: 100 acceptance queries, 24 concurrency, target 150ms p95 (stream-start and full-response).
2) Cold cache exploratory: 250 prompts, ramp to 250 rps, measure throughput curve and tail latency.
3) Peak spike: short 2-minute test with 120 concurrency to validate graceful degradation and fallback policies.

-- Artifacts I'll drop into the Drive folder: redwood_harness_instructions_v2.md, a sample JMeter-style load file, and a brief measurement worksheet.

Let me know if BrightCart requires different definitions (e.g., measuring only full-response p95). Also confirm whether you want model variant fallbacks whitelisted during runs (we can either fix model version or allow fallback; tradeoffs noted in the harness doc).

Ben Carter
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attached: redwood_harness_instructions_v2.md, brightcart_prompt_set_v1.csv

Perfect — thank you Ben and Emma. Quick decisions to keep momentum: 

- BrightCart: please confirm the 100-query acceptance bucket by EOD Monday (we can accept a csv with a column "acceptance=true").
- BrightCart: please indicate whether you want us to freeze model version for the acceptance run or allow automatic fallback (we recommend freezing for reproducibility).
- Redwood (Ben/Marissa): prepare the dry-run checklist and a calendar invite for Tue 2027-04-20 10:00am PT. Ben, include estimated GPU-hours and expected cost delta for quantized vs FP16 runs in the worksheet.

I'll schedule the dry-run once we have the confirmation items above. If we can't freeze model version, we'll include a deterministic seeding step in the harness so results are reproducible across runs.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
